svg.title: What USPS pages say about passport services: what a Post Office does, what it does not do, who applies in person, renewing by mail or online, appointments and what happens after you apply.
svg.text: USPS passport services
What the USPS pages say
What passport Post Offices do
Thousands of Post Offices accept first-time
applications; most of those also take photos.
The Postal Service reviews the application
and forwards it to the State Department.
What it does not do
Does not issue passports or hand them out;
they are mailed by the State Department.
No renewals in person (USPS.com). The FAQ
points renewals, lost or stolen passports and
name changes to the State Department.
Apply in person if (FAQ list)
First passport; child under 16; the last one
issued under 16 or over 15 years ago, or
lost, stolen or damaged; or a name change
you cannot document.
Renew by mail or online
USPS.com: if you can renew by mail or online,
you must; you cannot renew in person.
Expedited renewal service: by mail. Urgent
travel: USPS.com and the State Department
give different dates; check the State Dept.
A passport issued under 16 is not renewable.
Appointments
USPS.com: book online, at a lobby kiosk or a
retail counter; limited walk-in hours at select
locations. FAQ: also by phone. Renewals
cannot be booked in the scheduler.
After you apply
Processing starts when the State Department
gets the application. It mails the passport,
sometimes apart from your documents.
Sources: USPS.com passports page (no date) and
USPS FAQ (Nov. 5, 2026); read Nov. 13, 2026.
State Department pages: opened Nov. 13 in a translated
view, English not verified; check them there.
